explanation:
## What the grids are made of

All three train grids are a scatter (or a tiling) of colour‑4 shapes on a background of 2. The only change between input and output is that some 4‑cells become 8, and the fact sheet shows every change comes in matched pairs of "3 cells right" and "3 cells down" segments that cross in the middle — i.e. every changed region is a **plus sign**: a centre cell plus its four orthogonal neighbours.

Where are those pluses in the input? In pair 1 the plus at centre (5,9) sits inside a larger size‑8 blob; in pair 3 the pluses at (5,6) and (8,1) are parts of bigger diagonal‑ish 4‑shapes; in pair 2 each pair of pluses belongs to a size‑11 object. So the rule is not "recolour objects that are pluses" — it is "find every cell of colour 4 whose four orthogonal neighbours are also 4, and recolour that cell and its four neighbours to 8". Everything else is left alone, including 4‑cells that merely touch the plus (e.g. (3,8),(3,9),(4,8) in pair 1 stay 4).

## Checking it

I ran exactly this test — centre cell non‑background, all four orthogonal neighbours the same colour — on every train pair and the result matched the outputs cell for cell, with centres (5,9); the 3×3 lattice of nine centres in pair 2; and (5,6),(8,1) in pair 3. On the test input the same check finds six centres: (2,2), (7,2), (7,12), (12,7), (17,7), (17,17), and none of them are adjacent, so the pluses don't overlap and the order of painting does not matter.

The test grid is 22×22, which no train pair has, but the rule is purely local (a 3×3 neighbourhood test), so size doesn't matter; the colours are derived from the grid (background = most common colour, the plus colour is whatever the centre cell is) and only the output colour 8 is a constant shared by all pairs.

## Construction on the test input

Starting from the input canvas, for each of the six centres I paint the plus (centre + up/down/left/right) with 8 and emit a stage, so the student sees the pluses being stamped one at a time in reading order. The final canvas is returned.
